findings.title: Live client is `client/` (Bevy 0.18); `voxydust/` and `voxydust-next/` are DEAD and not in the workspace
findings.detail: The audit prompt names `voxydust/` and commits a172a6a/521ca50/c720010, but those commits landed in `client/`, not `voxydust/`. `voxydust/` is the original raw-wgpu/winit client (221k-byte main.rs, last source commit e8be8f6 on 2026-04-24) and is NOT a workspace member. `voxydust-next/` (also not a member) was a Bevy prototype/parking-lot whose lessons were ported into `client/`; its last touch was 521ca50 but only as a reference. The single live client is `client/` (workspace member, Bevy 0.18 + bevy_egui, last touched 2026-06-04). All transfer logic, ConnectionTask, dual-shard compositing, and interpolation live in `client/src/`. Any rebuild must target `client/` and can delete `voxydust/` + `voxydust-next/` outright (dead weight, ~300k+ lines of stale code in the tree).
findings.evidence: Cargo.toml members list (no voxydust); git log -1 voxydust/src=e8be8f6 (Apr 24), voxydust-next/src=521ca50 (May 22), client/src=e1a8d65 (Jun 4); voxydust/src/main.rs=221214 bytes vs client/src/main.rs=390 lines

findings.title: Transfer orchestration has ZERO behavioral test coverage
findings.detail: Every transfer-critical module has no unit tests: net/network.rs (the controller, 0), shard/registry.rs (0), shard/transition.rs (0), shard/worldstate.rs (0), shard/origin.rs (0), camera/pose.rs (0), remote/mod.rs (0). Tests exist only on pure leaf math: temporal_interp.rs (6), ship_pose.rs (10), connection.rs coalesce (7). The two client integration tests (tests/no_magic_numbers.rs, no_client_seed_derivation.rs) are source-lint guards, not behavioral. The entire race-condition-dense handoff/grace/promote/eviction machine — exactly what the user says 'doesn't work' — is validated only by manual play-testing. This is THE root reason transfers are 'hard to fix': there is no harness to reproduce a transfer race deterministically, so every fix is a guess verified by re-running the cluster.
findings.evidence: grep #[test]: network.rs=0, registry.rs=0, transition.rs=0, worldstate.rs=0, origin.rs=0, camera/pose.rs=0, remote/mod.rs=0; client/tests/ holds only lint guards

findings.title: Transfer state is smeared across ~6 plugins with brittle inter-plugin system ordering; no single owner
findings.detail: A shard transfer touches at least: NetworkBridgeSet (drain) -> ShardTransitionLatchSet (latch_transitions, grace capture) -> ShardRegistrySet (handle_disconnects, handle_connected, handle_secondary_connected, chained) -> WorldStateIngestSet (reset_on_shard_change, ingest) -> ShipPoseIngestSet/PlanetPoseIngestSet -> PlayerSyncSet (consume_spawn_pose_latch, apply_worldstate_pose) -> ShardOriginSet (refresh_origins, rebase) -> RemoteEntitiesSet -> CharacterRenderSet (reparent). The correctness of a transfer depends on exact `.before/.after/.chain()` ordering across these sets, and the code comments explicitly document multiple cases where the wrong order orphans the ship ChunkSource or graces the wrong shard (transition.rs:73-88, registry.rs:111-135). State that must stay coherent across a transfer (PrimaryShard, Secondaries, SourceIndex, GraceWindow, PendingSecondaryConnects, PrimaryWorldState, SecondaryWorldStates, ShipWorldPoseRegistry, SpawnPoseLatch, RemotePlayers, last_authoritative) lives in ~11 separate resources with no transactional update. A transfer is not an atomic operation anywhere; it is an emergent consequence of ordering.
findings.evidence: client/src/shard/transition.rs:73-113; client/src/shard/registry.rs:103-137; client/src/camera/pose.rs:104-142; ordering constraints documented in-line across all shard/*.rs plugins

findings.title: The code is a sediment of race-condition patches; comments are an archaeology of past breakage
findings.detail: The transfer modules are dominated by defensive workarounds layered over each other: PendingSecondaryConnects buffer (registry.rs:199-230) defers a SecondaryConnected that races a ShardHandoff; GraceWindow (transition.rs) keeps old ChunkSources alive 1.5s to mask re-stream gaps; the 'ignored SecondaryDisconnected for current primary (post-promote observer EOF)' guard (registry.rs:343-362) is the eviction-landmine/FIX-1; reset_on_shard_change defers secondary cleanup to ingest_primary to avoid a blink (worldstate.rs:147-196); the AuthTrack 1000ms shard-cooldown + 1500ms carry-forward in remote/mod.rs absorbs cross-shard projection races. Each is individually reasonable but collectively they form an unfalsifiable web — fixing one race re-opens another (the commit 5b78136 'Not fully working shard transfers' is the live state). This is implementation debt accreted because the underlying model lets shards' state arrive in any order with no sequencing primitive.

findings.title: Client networking is raw TCP+UDP, not QUIC — contradicts the stated architecture and is a structural source of handoff fragility
findings.detail: Despite the project description ('QUIC transport via quinn'), the client speaks raw tokio TcpStream + UdpSocket directly to shards (network.rs, connection.rs). There is no reliability/ordering layer: the controller hand-rolls length-prefixed framing, manual hole-punch hellos, 60s TCP keepalives, monotonic-tick guards to drop reordered UDP WorldStates, and a 'keepalive' sentinel passed as an Err string from recv_server_msg (connection.rs:377-381). Handoff control messages (ShardHandoff/PreConnect/Redirect) ride TCP and are explicitly forwarded from BOTH primary and secondary read paths 'to close a race' (connection.rs:861-933) because there is no stream/session abstraction guaranteeing they land on a defined channel. QUIC streams (or even one multiplexed reliable channel per shard) would eliminate an entire class of these races. The client/server transport mismatch is itself a finding.

findings.title: Stale/contradictory documentation in the load-bearing connection module
findings.detail: connection.rs's module doc (lines 50-57) states 'nothing calls it in production yet ... ready to be the migration target,' but network.rs:626 and :771 DO spawn run_connection for both Primary and Secondary modes — the migration landed (commit 25f06c5). A reader trusting the doc would conclude the legacy split-task path is live (it was deleted). Similarly transition.rs:14-20 references 'voxydust network.rs binds SYSTEM+GALAXY secondaries to session_cancel_tx' — a mechanism that no longer exists in the live client. In a codebase the user already struggles to reason about, doc-comments that describe a prior architecture actively mislead debugging.

findings.title: Dual-shard compositing is a per-frame f64 floating-origin recomposition, not a persistent composited world
findings.detail: There is no 'WorldState compositing' data structure; compositing is emergent. Each shard is a ChunkSource root entity with an f64 ShardOrigin; every frame refresh_origins_from_worldstate (origin.rs:171-312) recomputes each shard's system-space origin from the freshest authoritative pose (own-ship from ShipWorldPoseRegistry, secondaries from primary entities[] or secondary WS), then rebase_shard_transforms writes camera-relative f32 Transforms. Remote entities are placed either parented under their shard's ChunkSource OR as root-rebased visuals (origin≈0 or PLANET) to avoid f32 cancellation (character/render.rs:250-337). The model is coherent and is the genuinely clever core — but it means a transfer must keep ~4 independent WS streams' origins mutually consistent every frame, and any one going stale produces the documented km-scale blinks. This is the dual-shard seam the user feels.
findings.evidence: client/src/shard/origin.rs:171-398; client/src/shard/worldstate.rs:55-141 (resolve_game_time_now max-of-sources); client/src/character/render.rs:250-337 (RootRebaseVisual dual path)

findings.title: Game-time-indexed interpolation (521ca50) is the strongest, most reusable piece — keep it
findings.detail: temporal_interp::lerp_at_game_time is a clean, well-tested, allocation-free primitive funneled by 3 call sites (CameraWorldPos::pos_at_game_time, RemoteEntity::interpolated_pose_at_game_time, ShipPoseTrack::pose_at_game_time). The insight — interpolate cam.pos AND remote.position against the SAME server-authoritative game_time so the cross-shard subtraction lands on one simulation instant — is correct and is the right foundation for seamless multi-shard rendering. ship_pose.rs (10 tests) and temporal_interp.rs (6 tests) are the only well-tested transfer-adjacent code and embody the 'container-frame, read direct-from-authority' pattern correctly. A rebuild should preserve this primitive and the ShipWorldPoseRegistry/PlanetWorldPoseRegistry pattern verbatim.
findings.evidence: client/src/shard/temporal_interp.rs:58-80 + tests; client/src/shard/ship_pose.rs:110-288 + tests; consumers in origin.rs, remote/mod.rs:656-682, camera/pose.rs:366-411

findings.title: ConnectionTask abstraction (a172a6a) is well-designed and salvageable; the controller above it is the weak layer
findings.detail: run_connection unifies one TCP+UDP socket pair per shard with a ConnectionMode (Primary/Secondary/Demoting) flipped in-place via a biased tokio::select on a control mpsc — so a Secondary can be promoted to Primary with zero socket churn (the seamless-promote goal). The mode->behavior matrix is documented and the session-token retag-on-promote logic (connection.rs:550-585) correctly fixes the 'input routes to orphan observer' bug. This task layer is the right shape. The fragility lives ABOVE it in run_network's controller (network.rs:286-537), which juggles primary/secondaries/demoting maps with manual await-ordering and the 'keep full ActiveConn so control_tx stays open or the task self-exits early' footgun (network.rs:260-275). Keep ConnectionTask; rebuild the controller as an explicit transfer state machine.

findings.title: Renderer / meshing / lighting are large and almost entirely transfer-agnostic — keep wholesale
findings.detail: By subsystem LOC: hud 9175, character 5141, lighting 4076, shard_types 1197, interaction 985. The lighting pipeline (atmosphere, solar, eclipse, IBL, emitters, sky), HUD/tablet UI, and character skeletal/IK/anim/ragdoll rendering are pure consumers of resolved state and do not orchestrate transfers. The only transfer entanglement they have is reading PrimaryWorldState/SecondaryWorldStates resources and parenting under a ChunkSource — a thin, well-defined seam. Estimated split: of ~31.3k client LOC, roughly 5.5–6.5k is transfer-entangled (net/ 2173, shard/ 2919 minus pure-math ~750, camera/pose 809, remote 785, chunk/stream 572, parts of input) ≈ 18-21%; the remaining ~79-82% (lighting, hud, character render, shaders, interaction, shard_types rendering) is transfer-agnostic and survives a rebuild untouched.
findings.evidence: per-dir wc -l: hud=9175 character=5141 lighting=4076; transfer-entangled net=2173 + shard~2169(net of tested math) + camera/pose=809 + remote=785 + chunk/stream=572

findings.title: main.rs is tiny and non-coupled — transfer handling is already physically separable from rendering
findings.detail: client/src/main.rs is 390 lines: it is purely a plugin-registration manifest plus a camera spawn, cursor-grab, and a debug HUD window. It contains NO transfer logic. The plugin architecture means transfer concerns (NetworkPlugin, ShardRegistryPlugin, ShardTransitionPlugin, WorldStateIngestPlugin, ShipPoseIngestPlugin, ShardOriginPlugin) are already isolated from rendering plugins (LightingPlugin, HudPlugin, CharacterPlugin). The seam needed for 'rebuild transfer-first while keeping the renderer' already exists structurally — a rebuild can swap the shard/net plugin cluster while leaving the rendering plugins and their resource-read contracts (PrimaryWorldState, SecondaryWorldStates, SourceIndex, CameraWorldPos) in place. This dramatically lowers rebuild risk.
findings.evidence: client/src/main.rs:66-152 (plugin registration only); plugin isolation in client/src/shard/*.rs, client/src/net/bridge.rs

findings.title: Ship-exit 'hull trap' is server-authoritative; the client cannot fix it but must consume the spawn pose correctly
findings.detail: The client has no disembark geometry logic — exit is an input action_bit sent over UDP (input/mod.rs), and the destination spawn position is computed server-side and arrives as SpawnPose in ShardHandoff/Transitioning. The client only LATCHES and applies it (transition.rs latch_transitions -> camera/pose.rs consume_spawn_pose_latch:173-240). So the 'wedged inside the landed hull' bug is a server spawn-pose computation problem, not a client bug. BUT the client's consume_spawn_pose_latch has its own fragility: it applies eye-offset along the body up-axis, loses roll in the yaw/pitch decomposition (pose.rs:166-172), and extrapolates along SpawnPose.velocity for up to ~1.5s before the first WS (pose.rs:34-55, 277-298) — if the server's spawn pose is already inside the hull, the client faithfully renders the player inside it. Rebuild implication: spawn-pose handling needs a client-side 'first WS reconciliation' contract, and the server side is where the trap must actually be fixed.
findings.evidence: client/src/camera/pose.rs:173-240 (consume_spawn_pose_latch), :34-55 (SpawnExtrapolation); client/src/shard/transition.rs:118-200 (latch); input action path in client/src/input/mod.rs

findings.title: Lossy `by_shard_type` secondary index coexists with authoritative `by_shard_key`, inviting wrong-shard bugs
findings.detail: SecondaryWorldStates carries BOTH by_shard_type (HashMap<u8,...>, last-write-wins, collapses multiple ships of same type into one slot) and by_shard_key (HashMap<ShardKey,...>, authoritative). Many consumers (lighting, AR, atmosphere, eclipse) still read the lossy by_shard_type 'for backward-compat' (worldstate.rs:40-59), while remote-entity parenting was specifically migrated to by_shard_key after the lossy index caused 'EVA observer can't see in-ship players' (remote/mod.rs:250-291). This dual-index split is a standing trap: any new consumer that grabs by_shard_type silently breaks with >1 same-type secondary (common with multiple ships). A rebuild should delete by_shard_type and force all reads through ShardKey.
findings.evidence: client/src/shard/worldstate.rs:40-59, :260-273; client/src/shard/origin.rs:291-384 (find_secondary_pose ignores by_shard_type for ships); client/src/remote/mod.rs:250-291

findings.title: Origin staleness propagation: secondary origins are LEFT UNCHANGED on a missing lookup, by design — masks bugs as drift
findings.detail: refresh_origins_from_worldstate intentionally does NOT reset a secondary's origin to zero when no authoritative pose is found this tick (origin.rs:291-311), to avoid a snap-to-zero blink. Combined with grace extrapolation (drive_grace_transforms applies velocity*elapsed to graced sources, transition.rs:250-261) and the 1.5s carry-forward in remote/mod.rs, the client has THREE independent 'keep showing the last good position' mechanisms with different time windows (grace 1500ms, carry-forward 1500ms, auth-cooldown 1000ms, pose-track eviction 1500ms). When a transfer half-fails, the result is not a clean error but a slowly-drifting ghost that ages out over 1-1.5s — exactly the 'things sort of work then break weirdly' symptom that is hard to diagnose. These should be unified into one explicit staleness/lifetime model in a rebuild.

summary:
The audit target named in the prompt (`voxydust/`) is DEAD: it is the original raw-wgpu client, not a workspace member, last source-touched 2026-04-24. `voxydust-next/` is also dead (a Bevy prototype/parking-lot, not a member). The single LIVE client is `client/` (Bevy 0.18, ~31.3k LOC), and ALL the commits the prompt cites (a172a6a ConnectionTask, 521ca50 game-time interpolation, c720010 container-frame, the T0/T1/T2/T4 series, 5b78136 'Not fully working shard transfers') landed there. Delete the two dead crates in any rebuild.\n\nWHY TRANSFERS ARE FRAGILE (root causes, in order): (1) ZERO behavioral tests on the transfer machine — network.rs controller, registry, transition, worldstate, origin, camera/pose, remote all have 0 unit tests; only pure leaf math is tested. There is no way to reproduce a transfer race deterministically, so every fix is a guess. (2) A transfer is not an atomic operation anywhere — it is an emergent consequence of ~9 ECS system-sets firing in a precise `.before/.after/.chain` order, mutating ~11 independent resources (PrimaryShard, Secondaries, SourceIndex, GraceWindow, PendingSecondaryConnects, primary/secondary WorldStates, registries, latch, RemotePlayers/AuthTrack). (3) The code is sediment: PendingSecondaryConnects buffer, GraceWindow, the FIX-1 'ignore SecondaryDisconnected for current primary' guard, reset-deferral, and AuthTrack cooldowns are stacked race-patches where fixing one re-opens another. (4) Client transport is raw TCP+UDP (not QUIC), so handoff control messages must be redundantly forwarded from both primary and secondary read paths to dodge races a real stream/session layer would prevent.\n\nWHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD AND MUST BE KEPT: the ConnectionTask abstraction (mode-flip in-place, zero socket churn on promote) is correctly shaped — the weak layer is the controller above it. The game-time-indexed interpolation primitive + ShipWorldPoseRegistry/container-frame 'read-direct-from-authority' pattern is the clever, well-tested core of seamless multi-shard rendering. main.rs is a 390-line plugin manifest with no transfer logic, so transfer handling is ALREADY physically separable from rendering. Roughly 79-82% of client LOC (lighting 4.1k, hud 9.2k, character render/IK 5.1k, shaders, interaction, shard-type rendering) is transfer-agnostic and survives a rebuild untouched; only ~18-21% (net/, most of shard/, camera/pose, remote/, chunk/stream) is transfer-entangled.</summary>
<rebuild_implications>KEEP-AND-HARDEN is viable for ~80% of the client (renderer, meshing, lighting/atmosphere/eclipse shaders, HUD/tablet, character skeletal+IK+anim+ragdoll) — these are mature, transfer-agnostic, and already isolated behind Bevy plugins reading well-defined resource contracts. REBUILD-TRANSFER-FIRST should target ONLY the net/ + shard/ + camera-pose cluster (~6k LOC), keeping the multi-shard CONCEPT and these salvageable primitives: ConnectionTask (connection.rs), lerp_at_game_time (temporal_interp.rs), ShipWorldPoseRegistry/PlanetWorldPoseRegistry container-frame pattern, and the f64 floating-origin/ChunkSource rebase. The rebuilt foundation REQUIRES: (a) a single explicit transfer state machine that owns the handoff as an atomic, sequenced operation (current/observer/promoting/demoting) instead of emergent system-ordering; (b) a deterministic test harness that can drive a scripted transfer (PreConnect/Handoff/Promote/Demote/Disconnect in any interleaving) against in-memory channels — this is the highest-leverage missing piece and the direct cure for 'hard to fix what doesn't work'; (c) one unified staleness/lifetime model replacing the 4 overlapping grace/carry-forward/cooldown/eviction windows; (d) deletion of the lossy by_shard_type index in favor of ShardKey-only; (e) ideally moving the client transport to QUIC streams (matching the server) so handoff-control messages have a defined, race-free channel and the redundant dual-path forwarding can be deleted. The ship-exit hull trap is server-side (client only consumes SpawnPose) — fix on the server, but give the client a defined first-WS reconciliation contract for spawn-pose latching.</rebuild_implications>
